title: With common European indices, Finnish moth thermal composition followed an 18-year temperature mean fully, but British ECN moths showed 16% (95% CI -18% to 52%) of that rise in 1993-2015
abstract: Question: earlier campaign work found that Finnish moths are the main terrestrial exception to weak climate tracking: their community temperature index (CTI) followed about 100% of the spatial expectation. Is this a property of moths or of Finland? Data: UK Environmental Change Network light traps (11 sites, 233 site-years, 1993-2015) and the Finnish release of Ellis et al. 2025 (62 sites, 1993-2022). Method: one estimator; one European species temperature index (STI) source from GBIF density tiles and CRU TS 4.09 climate (r = 0.92 with the Ellis STIs); spatial slope of site CTI on temperature; trend (slow) and anomaly (fast) fractions; crossed site and year-block bootstrap. Planned result: inconclusive for Britain. British sites warmed only 0.10 C per decade (CI -0.32 to 0.50), so the British slow fraction was 0.26 (-0.87 to 1.42). Finland gave 1.01 (0.79 to 1.30), and 0.98-1.12 in all STI and weight variants, including STIs without Finnish cells. Fast fractions were small in both countries (0.02 and 0.05). The same 294 species sorted their trends by STI four times more weakly in Britain (difference CI -0.0077 to -0.0021 per year per C). Post hoc: no exponential lag gives the Finnish pair of fractions; a 18-20 year running mean of temperature with the full spatial slope comes close. Britain warmed before 1993, so memory models that fit the small fast response predict a British CTI rise of 0.007-0.011 C per year. The observed rise was 0.0017 (-0.0021 to 0.0055): 16% (-18% to 52%) of the 18-year prediction, and 0.16-0.27 for running means of 10-25 years and lag rates 0.05-0.2. Finland realised 1.29-2.05; all Britain-minus-Finland intervals were below -0.59. A trap-effort control gave a British share of 0.18 (0.03 to 0.35). Conclusion: the moth exception is not a general moth property; place-specific processes or a non-climatic Finnish trend remain possible. Limitations: 11 British sites; the informative British comparison depends on post hoc memory models with full spatial equivalence; grid temperature at upland sites; ECN effort changes; GBIF effort bias; the Finnish data overlap earlier studies.

Right: Britain (ECN) 1993-2015. The same memory model follows the Finnish CTI but predicts a British rise that did not occur.
Observed CTI trend divided by the trend that each temperature-memory model predicts with the full spatial slope, 1993-2015, with 95% bootstrap intervals. Dashed line: full realisation.

Fast (anomaly) and slow (trend) fractions. Points and clouds: observed estimates and bootstrap draws. Lines: fractions produced by exponential-lag and running-mean temperature models on the same site-years.

citations.reason: Reports the near-benchmark Finnish moth response; we reproduce it with independent GBIF indices and test whether it transfers to British moths.
Finnish presence and count indices near the spatial benchmark; our variants agree.
